sources.title: User-supplied Wan3.0 Prompt Tuner methodology
sources.usage: Independently implemented behavior and condensed writing guidance; supplied materials remain reference data.

sources.title: Alibaba Cloud Wan 3 official prompt and API documentation
sources.note: Current model metadata and current API documentation govern supported parameters and limits.

common: Start from the user's actual intent and visible source facts. Preserve quoted dialogue, explicit camera instructions and required outcome.
Each action span needs a start state, one visible main action, one camera behavior and an end state. Check that the next start follows the previous end.
For one continuous shot, state the actor route, camera route, contact objects and final composition. Keep the number and position of stationary structures stable.
Separate prompt-controlled intent from model capability risk. Physical contact, falls, liquids and complex forces can deform even with a good prompt.
Use concise observable target states. Writing heuristics such as positive wording are optional practices, not promises or protocol limits.
The image/reference already establishes appearance. Prefer motion, camera and intermediate action rather than repeating every surface detail.
Scene geometry, immutable objects, poses and contact points from source analysis must remain consistent with the chosen task.
Flag contradictions such as fixed camera plus fast orbit, changing time/place inside one stable shot, or too many actions for the selected duration.
Treat media roles as distinct. First/last-frame inputs and reference-mode inputs must be checked against the target model's actual supported combination.
Keep parameter suggestions separate from the usable prompt. Parameter suggestions never modify the user's generation request.

drama: Give each character an explicit spatial role, facing direction, gaze target and motive visible in the action. Preserve the axis across connected shots.
Favor a clear conflict, actor reaction and changed end state. A short generated segment should complete a small action rather than endlessly repeat gestures.
Natural acting uses breathing and small shifts of gaze. A sleep beat can close eyes once near the end; ordinary gaze should not be instructed to blink repeatedly.
For known dialogue, keep every word and speaker assignment. Mark on-screen speech versus off-screen voice, and use mouth-lock wording only for a genuinely silent/voice-over segment.
Describe actual light direction, focus and actor weight. Avoid adding dramatic camera moves, props or weather merely to make prose more cinematic.
For connected generation segments, the previous actual endpoint or the exact shared keyframe provides the next opening. A new independent composition is a deliberate edit, not seamless motion.
ecommerce: State the product's identity and the exact feature the user wants to demonstrate. Preserve its logo/name, silhouette, component layout and material boundaries.
Assign references specific duties such as product appearance, presenter identity, motion or camera. Do not blend unrelated roles.
Show one measurable benefit through a plausible action and visible result. Avoid inventing efficacy claims or an unsupported specification.
Keep handling and contact simple. Hands should grip the same surfaces throughout a demonstration, with product scale and orientation continuous.
For spoken selling points, preserve brand pronunciation and all required wording. Product evidence and voice-over belong to distinct content layers.
Choose composition and light that reveal the requested feature. An unrequested transformation, exploded view or stylized macro must be disclosed as an assumption.

text-to-video: Supply subject, scene, visible action, camera and required ending because no source image establishes them.
Keep unprovided creative choices recognizable in assumptions. Match action density to the current duration.
first-frame: Describe how the existing first frame moves forward. Preserve its geometry, cast, object count and source appearance.
Specify a simple action path and end state; the source frame is the visual ground truth.
first-last-frame: Describe only the feasible intermediate process that connects the supplied start and end.
Compare endpoint pose, object placement, scene and camera. Flag incompatible endpoints instead of inventing a morph to hide the gap.
A matching endpoint does not guarantee stable geometry during physical interaction. Keep contact and camera instructions simple.
reference: Use the supplied per-type numbered reference labels consistently. Images, videos and audio are numbered independently.
Declare each reference's role: identity/product, environment, motion/camera, style or voice.
Reference audio requires a supported role and a clear speaker/line assignment. It cannot override the target mode's media-combination rules.
v2v: Describe the edit target, time interval and requested change. Preserve the remaining source action, camera and appearance according to user intent.
Differentiate editing an existing action from extending a video. For extension, describe the additional event after the existing endpoint.
Use target model metadata to check video-input limits and timing. V2V is tuning intent, not an invented API mode parameter.

diagnosis: Return observed symptoms, evidence-based possible causes, the smallest useful prompt patch and a controlled retest.
Compare before/during/after the selected time interval. For warped stairs, inspect edge lines, number and spacing of steps, camera position and foot/hand contact points.
Distinguish source-frame conflict, overloaded or contradictory prompt, model capability limits, and unsupported API/media configuration.
For repeated blinking, replace repetitive eye-action wording with stable gaze and one explicit closing event when needed.
For background or geometry deformation during a fall/contact, simplify contact, use a smaller visible action, split at a meaningful edit or show a result state. Do not claim guaranteed repair.
For extra actors, props, cutaways or overlays, check source media facts and speech/edit instructions before appending long exclusion lists.
For unwanted environment rendering, describe the intended local material state and its spatial boundary. Avoid turning one local effect into an entire-scene weather event.
Retest one change at a time with the same approved source media and comparable parameters. Record what changed and inspect the actual interval.
audio: Separate environmental sound, character speech and music when the user requests audio control.
If audio output is disabled, preserve that parameter as read-only context. Do not invent dialogue or voice identity from unheard audio.
Voice reference observations require actual accessible audio and a capable analysis model. Otherwise mark the voice facts as unverified.
Keep a character's speaker/voice association near its dialogue. Silent acting and off-screen narration must be identified per shot.
